topology: 2 nodes x 4 H100, 8 MPI ranks, 1 GPU per rank, OpenMPI 4.1.5 over UCX 1.20.0 over NDR InfiniBand
why: A third-party MD code whose halo-exchange pattern follows from its own source: the processor grid is fixed on the command line, CommBrick exchanges with its face neighbours and with nobody else, and `-pk kokkos gpu/aware on|off` provably does not change WHICH messages are sent — only which memory they are sent from. That makes both the topology and the knob's null effect derivable before the capture exists.
workload_note: Every number above is an INPUT, not a reading. `ranks/nodes/tasks_per_node` are the sbatch and mpirun lines; `procgrid_*` is the `processors 2 2 2` line in in.lj; `steps/atoms/lattice_cells/reneighbour_every` are in.lj. The three derived ones: (1) halo_peers_per_rank = 3, because src/comm_brick.cpp:351 sets nswap = 2*(maxneed[0]+maxneed[1]+maxneed[2]) and for this box maxneed[d] = int(cutghost[d]*procgrid[d]/prd[d])+1 = int(2.8*2/67.19)+1 = 1 in every dimension, so six swaps, and with procgrid[d]=2 the left and right neighbour in a dimension are the SAME rank -> three distinct peers; (2) internode_peers_per_rank = 1, because src/procmap.cpp ProcMap::cart_map calls MPI_Cart_create with reorder=0, so rank = 4*cx + 2*cy + cz, and `--map-by ppr:4:node` puts ranks 0-3 on one node and 4-7 on the other, making cx the node index and the x-neighbour the only off-node face neighbour; (3) uses_managed_memory = 0, established from the build and the binary before any capture existed — see REPORT.md section A. halo_min_bytes = 4096 separates the halo (~64 kB/message: 32000 atoms/rank, ghost slab 2.8/33.6 of the subdomain, 24 B/ghost atom) from LAMMPS's thermo Allreduces (8-64 B), and names no identifier the run produced.
not_covered: ib_post_send and ib_poll_cq are expected EMPTY and are deliberately not in expect_tables. UCX's mlx5 transports build their send WQEs and ring the doorbell themselves, so ibv_post_send is not on the path; this is the same measurement PLAN-20260815-1540 Stage 3 recorded for job 44635003, reproduced here by a third-party application rather than by a microbenchmark. The consequence is that `comm_edges` — built in pcomm-read/link_sql.hpp:1112 from ib_post_send / mlx5_device_send / gpu_access only — is EMPTY for this workload, and the rank matrix has to be assembled from the UCX records by hand. gpumem/p2p is not run: NVBit costs ~8 min of module processing and this case is about the network layer.
cost_note: Four captured runs plus two bare runs in one allocation. LAMMPS itself is seconds; the allocation is sized by the export and the SQL, not the science.

expect_fail_asserts.peer_rank_resolvable: pcomm hooks ucp_worker_get_address (providers/ucx/ucx_hooks.hpp:181) and not ucp_worker_query. OpenMPI 4.1.5's mca_pml_ucx -- the two-sided path every LAMMPS halo message takes -- obtains its worker address through ucp_worker_query with UCP_WORKER_ATTR_FIELD_ADDRESS (ompi/mca/pml/ucx/pml_ucx.c:95-99) and does not import ucp_worker_get_address at all; only mca_osc_ucx does. So the one ucx_worker_address row per rank belongs to the ONE-SIDED worker, which carries no application traffic, and the PML endpoints' remote_prefix_hash matches nothing. Measured on the login-node shakeout: rank 0's 81-send / 3.13 MB endpoint has remote_prefix_hash 16991725616488086498, present in no ucx_worker_address row in the capture. See REPORT.md finding 2.
expect_fail_asserts.halo_peer_fanout: Same cause as peer_rank_resolvable: with no worker address for the PML worker there are zero RESOLVABLE peers, not three. The claim about LAMMPS is not in doubt and is not left unchecked -- halo_endpoint_fanout asserts the same fan-out of 3 in endpoint space, where no cross-rank join is needed, and it passes. This one stays as the marker for the missing rank attribution.

vacuous_without.note: halo_peers_grid_adjacent, halo_symmetric and no_self_halo are negative checks over the peer-resolved edge relation. That relation is EMPTY on this stack, so all three report no offending rows and assert nothing. They are deliberately left unmarked rather than marked expect_fail -- they do not fail -- and peer_rank_resolvable is the companion guard that makes their vacuity visible instead of silent. When the ucp_worker_query hook lands they become real checks with no edit.
